references.text: God answers the people's fear that their children would become plunder – He promises that it is precisely the children who will enter the land.
Moses recounts how God promised that the children, whom they feared would become plunder, would inherit the land.
The people complained earlier in Egypt and asked if it was because there were no graves there that they were brought out to die in the wilderness – the same pattern of complaint and desire to return.
The people complained that they were brought out into the wilderness to die and wished to return to Egypt – similar complaints and lack of trust.
The people longed to return to Egypt and the food they had there – the same theme of wanting to go back.
Korah and his followers accused Moses of bringing them out to let them die in the wilderness – a repetition of the accusation that the Lord brought them out to kill them.
A prophecy that Israel will be brought back to Egypt as punishment – an ironic connection to their desire to return.
Stephen refers to how the fathers would not obey Moses but pushed him away and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
